title: Optimization Problem Solving Pipeline
description: Takes a natural-language decision problem through formal modeling, routes it to the right solution method by problem class, evaluates solution quality, iterates on the model if the solution is infeasible or suboptimal, and gates final release behind analyst sign-off.
yaml:
apiVersion: ladder.dev/v1alpha1
kind: Workflow
metadata:
  name: optimization-problem-solving-pipeline
  title: Optimization Problem Solving Pipeline
  description: Takes a natural-language decision problem through formal modeling, routes it to the
    right solution method by problem class, evaluates solution quality, iterates on the model if the
    solution is infeasible or suboptimal, and gates final release behind analyst sign-off.
  version: 1.0.0
spec:
  objective: "Takes a natural-language decision problem through formal modeling, routes it to the
    right solution method by problem class, evaluates solution quality, iterates on the model if the
    solution is infeasible or suboptimal, and gates final release behind analyst sign-off. Trigger:
    user submits a decision problem in natural language (objective + constraints)"
  policies:
    maxConcurrency: 4
    onFailure: stop
    requireApprovalFor:
      - n9
  nodes:
    - id: n1
      kind: input
      name: Problem Intake
      summary: Problem Intake
      inputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - text
        properties:
          text:
            type: string
            description: The user's objective, source text, or instructions.
          workflowFields:
            type: object
            required:
              - objective_function
              - constraints
              - decision_variables
              - variable_domain_hints
            properties:
              objective_function: {}
              constraints: {}
              decision_variables: {}
              variable_domain_hints: {}
        x-ladder-input-mode: text
    - id: n2
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-opt-01
      name: Formulate Optimization Model
      summary: Formulate Optimization Model
      role: Operations research analyst specializing in translating real-world decision problems into
        formal optimization models.
      prompt: You are an Optimization Modeler agent. Given a natural-language description of a decision
        problem, you elicit and formalize the objective function, decision variables, and
        constraints into a precise mathematical model, and you classify the resulting model (linear,
        convex nonlinear, mixed-integer/combinatorial) so it can be routed to the right solution
        method. You actively flag ambiguous or missing constraints — an unstated capacity limit, an
        implicit non-negativity requirement — rather than silently guessing at intent, since a wrong
        formulation produces a confidently wrong "optimal" answer to the wrong problem.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evidence-verification
          - domain-analysis
          - quantitative-analysis
          - optimization
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n3
      kind: condition
      name: Route by Problem Class
      summary: Route from formulated model.problem class.
      config:
        expression: formulated_model.problem_class selects one declared branch
        branches:
          - label: linear
            when: linear
          - label: convex nonlinear
            when: convex_nonlinear
          - label: combinatorial mip
            when: combinatorial_mip
          - label: Default
            when: default
    - id: n4a
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-opt-02
      name: Solve as Linear Program
      summary: Solve as Linear Program
      role: Operations research engineer selecting and applying the right solution method
        (LP/NLP/MIP/heuristic) for a formulated model.
      prompt: You are an Optimization Solver agent. Given a formulated model, you select a solution method
        appropriate to its structure — simplex or interior-point for linear programs,
        gradient/interior-point methods for convex nonlinear programs, branch-and-bound or
        metaheuristics for combinatorial/MIP problems — and either run it or reason through it
        analytically for small enough cases. You report the solution's feasibility status, the
        optimality gap for MIP or heuristic methods (never presenting a heuristic result as provably
        optimal), and sensitivity information (shadow prices, binding constraints) when it's
        relevant to the decision the user is actually trying to make.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - optimization
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n4b
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-opt-02
      name: Solve as Convex/Nonlinear Program
      summary: Solve as Convex/Nonlinear Program
      role: Operations research engineer selecting and applying the right solution method
        (LP/NLP/MIP/heuristic) for a formulated model.
      prompt: You are an Optimization Solver agent. Given a formulated model, you select a solution method
        appropriate to its structure — simplex or interior-point for linear programs,
        gradient/interior-point methods for convex nonlinear programs, branch-and-bound or
        metaheuristics for combinatorial/MIP problems — and either run it or reason through it
        analytically for small enough cases. You report the solution's feasibility status, the
        optimality gap for MIP or heuristic methods (never presenting a heuristic result as provably
        optimal), and sensitivity information (shadow prices, binding constraints) when it's
        relevant to the decision the user is actually trying to make.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - optimization
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n4c
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-opt-02
      name: Solve as Combinatorial/MIP
      summary: Solve as Combinatorial/MIP
      role: Operations research engineer selecting and applying the right solution method
        (LP/NLP/MIP/heuristic) for a formulated model.
      prompt: You are an Optimization Solver agent. Given a formulated model, you select a solution method
        appropriate to its structure — simplex or interior-point for linear programs,
        gradient/interior-point methods for convex nonlinear programs, branch-and-bound or
        metaheuristics for combinatorial/MIP problems — and either run it or reason through it
        analytically for small enough cases. You report the solution's feasibility status, the
        optimality gap for MIP or heuristic methods (never presenting a heuristic result as provably
        optimal), and sensitivity information (shadow prices, binding constraints) when it's
        relevant to the decision the user is actually trying to make.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - optimization
          - domain-analysis
          - decision-analysis
          - image-understanding
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: n5
      kind: join
      name: Reconverge After Solve
      summary: Reconverge After Solve
      config:
        join: first
    - id: n6
      kind: evaluate
      inlineRole: true
      name: Score Solution Quality
      summary: Evaluate feasibility and optimality gap.
      role: Deterministic metric evaluator
      prompt: Evaluate the upstream result using feasibility and optimality gap. Return a score, pass/fail
        verdict, evidence, uncertainty, and the smallest corrective action. Do not claim
        programmatic measurement unless the host supplies the required tool.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - evaluation
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors: []
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
        required:
          - score
          - passed
          - reasons
        properties:
          score:
            type: number
          passed:
            type: boolean
          reasons:
            type: array
            items:
              type: string
      config:
        threshold: 0.8
    - id: n7
      kind: condition
      name: Meets Acceptance Criteria
      summary: Meets Acceptance Criteria
      config:
        expression: solution_score.feasible AND solution_score.optimality_gap < 0.01
        branches:
          - label: "True"
            when: "true"
          - label: "False"
            when: "false"
    - id: n_loop
      kind: loop
      name: Refine Model Until Converged
      summary: Repeat a bounded revision sequence until solution_score meets acceptance criteria.
      config:
        body:
          - n2
          - n3
          - n4a
          - n4b
          - n4c
          - n5
          - n6
          - n7
        exitCondition: solution_score meets acceptance criteria
        maxIterations: 5
        onExhausted: stop
    - id: n9
      kind: approval
      name: Analyst Sign-off on Final Solution
      summary: Pause for requesting analyst / decision owner; on timeout, escalate.
    - id: n10
      kind: agent
      templateRef: math-gen-02
      name: Generate Solution Report & Sensitivity Plot
      summary: Generate Solution Report & Sensitivity Plot
      role: Mathematical visualization specialist producing accurate, legible plots and geometric
        diagrams.
      prompt: You are a Math Visualization & Graphing Agent. You produce plots of functions, parametric
        and polar curves, vector fields, and geometric constructions, always accurately labeled with
        axes, scale, and critical features (roots, extrema, asymptotes, inflection points) rather
        than a bare unlabeled curve. You choose the visualization type suited to what the user is
        actually trying to understand — a phase portrait for a dynamical system, a contour plot for
        a two-variable optimization landscape, a unit-circle diagram for a trig identity — rather
        than defaulting to a generic line plot for everything.
      capabilities:
        skills:
          - privacy-review
          - image-understanding
          - domain-analysis
        tools:
          - read
          - calculate
        connectors:
          - api:desmos
        permissions:
          - read-only
      outputSchema:
        type: object
    - id: workflow-output
      kind: output
      name: Validated result
      summary: Return the completed optimization problem solving pipeline deliverable, validation
        evidence, and unresolved uncertainty.
  edges:
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-1
      from: n1
      to: n2
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-2
      from: n2
      to: n3
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-3
      from: n3
      to: n4a
      kind: control
      condition: linear
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-4
      from: n3
      to: n4b
      kind: control
      condition: convex_nonlinear
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-5
      from: n3
      to: n4c
      kind: control
      condition: combinatorial_mip
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-6
      from: n4a
      to: n5
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-7
      from: n4b
      to: n5
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-8
      from: n4c
      to: n5
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-9
      from: n5
      to: n6
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-10
      from: n6
      to: n7
      kind: data
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-11
      from: n7
      to: n9
      kind: control
      condition: "true"
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-12
      from: n7
      to: n_loop
      kind: control
      condition: "false"
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-13
      from: n_loop
      to: n9
      kind: control
      condition: loop_exit
    - id: wf-math-01-edge-14
      from: n9
      to: n10
      kind: control
      condition: approved
    - id: wf-math-01-output-1
      from: n10
      to: workflow-output
      kind: dependency
